name: Burn (Tracel Rust deep learning framework)
notable_features: The pitch is not speed, it is ELIMINATING THE EXPORT STEP. The README's argument is that the standard pipeline (train in Python, export to ONNX or optimise for vLLM/ONNX Runtime/TensorRT) is 'often brittle and lossy, ruling out complex architectures', so Burn lets the training code itself be the inference code. That is a genuinely different goal from every other framework in this repo and it is the reason to know about Burn

JIT kernel fusion with dynamic shapes: PyTorch-like dynamic graphs and eager ergonomics, but tensor-op streams are compiled so adjacent ops fuse. The stated benefit is flexibility without the usual dynamic-graph performance cliff

Incremental compilation is the research-usability argument: the README claims sub-5-second recompiles even in release mode, aimed squarely at the 'long Rust compile times killed my edit-compile-run loop' objection
Explicitly aimed at on-device personalization and federated learning, where the train/serve code-identity property actually pays off and where ONNX export is genuinely lossy
Broadest declared backend spread in this niche - topics name cuda, rocm, metal, vulkan, wasm and webgpu in one project
MIT OR Apache-2.0, 16020 stars, 1075 forks, only 216 open issues, created 2022-07-18, last push 2026-10-02, not archived, homepage burn.dev
hardware_caveats: NO PUBLISHED INFERENCE THROUGHPUT. No tok/s, no TTFT, no comparison against llama.cpp, vLLM or SGLang appears in the README or the project pages. Burn is a framework and its published numbers, where they exist, are training-side. Any inference throughput attributed to Burn is third-party and should be treated as unverified

NO SCHEDULER. No continuous batching, no paged KV, no prefix caching, no chunked prefill - same structural position as candle. It is a batch-1 tensor library with a training story, not a serving system
NO GGUF AND NO QUANTISATION ZOO. safetensors natively, ONNX for import. Nothing in the AWQ/GPTQ/EXL2/Marlin family. If quantised inference is the requirement this is the wrong project

The JIT fusion story is the performance bet and it is unproven against hand-tuned kernels for LLM decode specifically. Fusing elementwise and normalisation ops around GEMMs is exactly the case llama.cpp and TensorRT-LLM already handle with hand-written kernels
It is not an LLM serving engine: no tokenizer pipeline, no OpenAI-compatible server, no request scheduling. Anything the README calls 'inference' is a forward pass you call from your own program
JIT compilation introduces a warm-up and a compile surface that is awkward for a serverless or FaaS deployment model where cold start is already the dominant latency term
best_for: A team that trains a model in Rust and wants to ship that exact model, particularly on-device personalization or federated learning where an export round-trip is unacceptable
Portability across CPU/CUDA/ROCm/Metal/Vulkan/WASM/WebGPU from one codebase, including a web target
Anyone blocked by a lossy ONNX export of an architecture the mainstream exporters do not support
A research loop where recompile time is the bottleneck - the sub-5-second claim is specifically for that
avoid_for: Serving LLMs to multiple concurrent users - no scheduler exists
Anyone optimising for tokens per second: no published inference numbers and a JIT fusion bet that has not been shown to beat purpose-built kernels
Reusing GGUF or existing quantised weights - the formats are not supported
Teams wanting a drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoint - it is a library
notes: The second Rust framework in this slice and the more interesting of the two, because its stated reason to exist is a property - train-and-serve code identity - that no CUDA-shaped serving engine offers. Included to make the point that the Rust answer to inference splits into three different layers: [[niche-candle]] as a minimal library, burn as a full train-and-deploy framework, and the Rust SERVER layer ([[text-generation-inference]], [[triton-inference-server]]). NO PUBLISHED INFERENCE THROUGHPUT - recorded as an explicit negative rather than filled with an estimate.
